source_refs.note: Exercise 7.1, Question 5 (book p. 230); the book prints no answers for Exercise 7.1; answers checked with sympy and the solution book

blocks.prompt: 5 (a) Figure 7.12 shows the velocity-time graph of an object moving in a straight line over a 12-second time interval. At what time did the object change its direction of motion?
blocks.explanation:
The sign of the velocity gives the direction of motion.
Given: the graph of Figure 7.12. To find: when v changes sign.
Plan: find where the falling line from (5, 4) to (10, -2) cuts the time axis.
steps:
Given: the velocity-time graph through (0, 0), (3, 4), (5, 4), (10, -2), (12, -2). The figure prints no units; we take v in m/s and t in s.
To find: the time at which the direction changes.
Method: v > 0 means forward and v < 0 means backward, so the object turns round where v = 0 and changes sign.

Slope of the falling line
\[m = \dfrac{-2 - 4}{10 - 5} = -\dfrac{6}{5}\]
Why: slope through the two corner points (5, 4) and (10, -2).

Equation of the line
\[v - 4 = -\dfrac{6}{5}(t - 5)\]
Why: point-slope form with the point (5, 4).

Put \(v = 0\)
\[t - 5 = 4 \times \dfrac{5}{6} = \dfrac{10}{3}\]
\[t = \dfrac{25}{3} \approx 8.33\]
Why: at the turning instant the velocity is zero. The figure itself marks 25/3 on the time axis.

Check
\[4 - \dfrac{6}{5}\left(\dfrac{25}{3} - 5\right) = 4 - 4 = 0 \;\checkmark\]
Why: at t = 10 there is only a corner: v stays at -2, still negative, so the object keeps moving backward there; only the acceleration changes.

blocks.prompt: 5 (b) Figure 7.12 shows the velocity-time graph of an object moving in a straight line over a 12-second time interval. Calculate the total distance travelled and the displacement of the object during the 12 seconds.
blocks.explanation:
Distance and displacement both come from areas under the velocity-time graph.
Given: area A1 above the time axis, area A2 below it.
Plan: by the Note of 7.1.5, distance = A1 + A2 and displacement = A1 - A2.
steps:
Given: the graph of Figure 7.12 and the turning time t = 25/3 from part (a).
To find: the total distance and the displacement in 12 s.
Method: Note (7.1.5): with \(A_1\) the area above the time axis and \(A_2\) the area below, displacement \(= A_1 - A_2\) and distance \(= A_1 + A_2\). Each area is split into triangles and rectangles.

Area above the axis, \(0 \le t \le \frac{25}{3}\)
\[\tfrac{1}{2}(3)(4) = 6\]
\[2 \times 4 = 8\]
\[\tfrac{1}{2}\left(\tfrac{10}{3}\right)(4) = \tfrac{20}{3}\]
\[A_1 = 6 + 8 + \tfrac{20}{3} = \tfrac{62}{3}\]
Why: triangle from 0 to 3, rectangle from 3 to 5, triangle from 5 to \(\frac{25}{3}\) (base \(\frac{25}{3} - 5 = \frac{10}{3}\)).

Area below the axis, \(\frac{25}{3} \le t \le 12\)
\[\tfrac{1}{2}\left(\tfrac{5}{3}\right)(2) = \tfrac{5}{3}\]
\[2 \times 2 = 4\]
\[A_2 = \tfrac{5}{3} + 4 = \tfrac{17}{3}\]
Why: triangle from \(\frac{25}{3}\) to 10 (base \(\frac{5}{3}\), height 2), rectangle from 10 to 12. We take the size of the area; the minus sign is used in the next step.

Distance and displacement
\[\text{Distance} = \tfrac{62}{3} + \tfrac{17}{3} = \tfrac{79}{3}\]
\[\approx 26.33\text{ m}\]
\[\text{Displacement} = \tfrac{62}{3} - \tfrac{17}{3} = 15\text{ m}\]
Why: distance adds both areas; displacement subtracts the backward part.

Check with trapeziums
\[A_1 = \tfrac{1}{2}\left(\tfrac{25}{3} + 2\right)(4) = \tfrac{62}{3} \;\checkmark\]
\[A_2 = \tfrac{1}{2}\left(\tfrac{11}{3} + 2\right)(2) = \tfrac{17}{3} \;\checkmark\]
Why: each region is also a trapezium (parallel sides \(\frac{25}{3}\) and 2, and \(12 - \frac{25}{3} = \frac{11}{3}\) and 2).
blocks.final_answer: Distance \(= \frac{79}{3} \approx 26.33\) m; displacement \(= 15\) m (in the forward direction)
